# Backend Slop Audit + DDD Domain Map (Baseline First)

## Objective

Inventory and diagnose “AI slop” in the backend codebase and produce a Domain-Driven Design (DDD) modularization plan grounded in evidence (hotspots, duplication, boundary violations). Do not do a big rewrite yet; this task is baseline + plan only.

## Context

The backend was vibe-coded. We need to identify what “slop” actually is in this repository before making major architectural changes. The output of this task becomes the spec for the DDD refactor task.

## Requirements

1. Detect and report slop hotspots (evidence-based):

   * Top 20 largest files/classes/modules by LOC
   * God services (business logic + I/O + orchestration + formatting in one place)
   * Duplicate logic (validation, mapping, fee math, corridor parsing, provider normalization, error handling)
   * Inconsistent patterns (DTOs, error responses, logging, retry/timeout, caching, pagination)
   * Circular or undesirable imports / dependency cycles (if present)
2. Map current backend architecture:

   * Language/framework/runtime (Node/.NET/Python/etc.)
   * Service topology (monolith vs microservices; boundaries if multiple services)
   * API style (REST/tRPC/GraphQL/etc.) and routing layout
   * Data stores (Postgres/Redis/etc.), access patterns, migrations
   * Background processing (queues, cron, workers)
   * Auth/session model (if any)
   * Observability (logging, metrics, traces) and current gaps
3. Propose bounded contexts (5–8 domains) based on actual code and user/business flows. Example candidates:

   * Quote Ingestion
   * Normalization / Canonicalization
   * Pricing Metrics (NDV, TEER, RCI, RVI, suppression rules)
   * Corridor Registry
   * Provider Registry
   * User/Auth (if present)
   * Analytics/Audit/Experiments
   * Admin/Ops
4. Recommend a target folder/module structure aligned with DDD layers:

   * domain (entities, value objects, invariants; pure logic)
   * application (use-cases, orchestration, transactions)
   * infrastructure (DB/Redis/HTTP clients/queues)
   * interfaces (controllers/handlers/DTOs)
     Include a small public export surface for each bounded context (index file).
5. Define hard dependency rules and how to enforce them (lint/build-time where possible):

   * interfaces → application → domain
   * infrastructure implements ports used by application
   * domain must not depend on frameworks, DB, HTTP, Redis
   * shared-kernel must not import domain modules
6. Identify 3 “golden patterns” to standardize backend development. Examples:

   * A unified error model (typed errors + consistent HTTP mapping)
   * A request context pattern (correlation ID + logging + tracing)
   * A port/adapter pattern for external providers (strict interfaces + test fixtures)

## Constraints

* Do not perform a big refactor in this task.
* You may add small non-invasive analysis helpers (scripts) if needed.
* No externally visible behavior changes in this task.
* Outputs must be concrete and repo-specific.

## Deliverables

Write the following Markdown docs under `/docs/refactor/`:

* docs/refactor/backend-baseline.md
* docs/refactor/backend-slop-inventory.md
* docs/refactor/backend-ddd-domain-map.md
* docs/refactor/backend-refactor-plan.md
* docs/refactor/backend-golden-patterns.md

Each doc must include file paths and evidence, not general advice.

## Success Criteria

The task is complete when:

* [ ] A backend baseline report exists (stack, topology, data stores, queues, auth, observability)
* [ ] A slop inventory exists with top hotspots and why each is slop (with paths)
* [ ] A duplication map identifies repeated patterns and where they occur
* [ ] A DDD domain map proposes 5–8 bounded contexts tied to actual backend features
* [ ] A target folder/module structure is proposed with dependency rules
* [ ] A prioritized refactor plan (10–20 slices) is produced with measurable wins per slice
* [ ] A golden-patterns spec is produced for 3 standard patterns to enforce across the backend

## Notes

Slop definitions (use these):

* God modules: >400 LOC with multiple responsibilities
* Cross-cutting duplication: same code pattern copied 3+ places
* Hidden coupling: services importing DB/client internals directly instead of via interfaces
* Inline mapping/formatting: DTO ↔ domain mapping scattered across endpoints
* Inconsistent errors/logging: different shapes/messages per endpoint

Start by inspecting the repository and listing:

* backend entrypoints and routing
* top 10 largest modules/classes
* the 3 most duplicated concerns
* the tightest coupling points you will break in the refactor plan

---

The orchestrator will continue iterations until limits are reached.
